title: Many Kinds of Families
bigQuestion: What makes a family a family?

story.title: Sunday Dinner at Grandma's Table
story.kicker: Come to Sunday dinner in Chicago. Three kinds of family sit at one table.
paragraphs: It is Sunday in Chicago. Rosa walks up the steps of a brick house. She smells rice and beans. She hears a lot of voices. Grandma opens the door. She gives Rosa a big hug.
The table is long. Grandpa sits at one end. Mom and Dad sit near him. Rosa sits by her baby brother. Aunt Luz and Uncle Tom are here too. So are cousins Ben and Mia.
Grandma is old. Rosa is young. Baby Sam is very new. That makes three groups of ages. We call each group a generation. Three generations eat at one table today.
Everyone has a job. Rosa sets the forks. Ben pours water. Grandpa tells a funny story. They all pass the food. They laugh together. This is Rosa's family.
story.think: Who sits at your table for a big meal? What job could you do to help?

lessons.title: Families Come in Many Sizes
lessons.mainIdea: Some families are big. Some families are small. All of them are families.
reading: Kai lives with his dad. That is two people. Lena lives with her mom, dad, and four sisters. That is seven people. Both are families.
A *family* is a group of people who belong together. They care for each other. A family can be two people. A family can be many people.
Some children live with a mom. Some live with a dad. Some live with a grandma or an aunt. Some live with both parents. Each one is a real family.

words.d: a group of people who belong together and care for each other

look.title: Two Doors on One Street
look.text: Look at the green door. A mom and one girl live there. Now look at the blue door. A grandpa, two parents, and three boys live there. Both homes have people who love each other.
look.prompt: Count the people behind each door. Are both groups families? Why?

check.q: How many people does Kai's family have?
check.why: Kai lives with his dad. That is two people.

choices: A group of people who belong together and care for each other
People who live on the same street
check.why: The reading says a family is a group who belong together and care for each other. It can be big or small.

check.q: Lena has a mom, a dad, and four sisters. Is that a family?
check.why: A family can be many people. Lena's group is a family.

lessons.title: Cousins, Aunts and Uncles
lessons.mainIdea: Your family can reach past your home to cousins, aunts, and uncles.
reading: Rosa has an Aunt Luz. Aunt Luz is her mom's sister. Rosa has an Uncle Tom too. He is married to Aunt Luz. Their children are Ben and Mia.
Ben and Mia are Rosa's *cousins*. A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle. Your aunt is your parent's sister. Your uncle is your parent's brother.
Cousins may live far away. They may live next door. Many families meet for holidays and birthdays. Cousins get to play together then.

words.d: the child of your aunt or uncle
the sister of your mom or dad, or your uncle's wife

look.title: A Family Tree Picture
look.text: Look at a picture of a tree. Grandma and Grandpa are at the bottom by the roots. Two branches grow up. One branch is Mom. The other branch is Aunt Luz. Little leaves grow on each branch. Rosa is a leaf on Mom's branch. Ben and Mia are leaves on Aunt Luz's branch.
look.prompt: Find Rosa's leaf. Find Ben's leaf. Why are they cousins?

check.why: Aunt Luz is the sister of Rosa's mom. That makes her Rosa's aunt.

choices: The child of your aunt or uncle
check.why: The reading says a cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.
Your uncle is your parent's brother.

lessons.title: Grandparents at Home
lessons.mainIdea: In many places, grandparents and grandchildren live in one home.
reading: In Mexico, Grandma Ana lives with her son and his children. She makes tortillas in the morning. Her grandson Luis helps. He likes to flip them.
Many homes around the world have three *generations*. A generation is a group of people about the same age. Grandparents, parents, and children are three generations.
You can find homes like this in Mexico. You can find them in India, Italy, and Korea. You can find them in Chicago too. Not every family lives this way. Many do.

words.d: a group of people in a family who are about the same age, like all the grandparents
the mom or dad of your mom or dad

look.title: Morning in a Busy Home
look.text: Look at the kitchen. Grandpa reads to a small girl. Mom packs lunches. Dad pours milk. A big boy ties his shoes. Grandma waters a plant by the window. Everyone is busy. Everyone is together.
look.prompt: Point to each generation. How many do you see?

check.q: What does Luis help Grandma Ana do?
check.why: Grandma Ana makes tortillas. Luis likes to flip them.

check.q: Grandparents, parents, and children make how many generations?
check.why: The reading says grandparents, parents, and children are three generations.

check.q: Where can you find grandparents living with grandchildren?
choices: In many places, like India, Italy, Korea, and Chicago
check.why: The reading names many places. Homes like this are found around the world.

lessons.title: What Grandparents Share
lessons.mainIdea: Grandparents often share stories, skills, and care with children.
reading: In Korea, a grandmother may teach a child to fold dumplings. In Italy, a grandfather may show how to plant tomatoes. In India, a grandmother may tell old stories at bedtime.
Grandparents know a lot. They remember long ago. They can pass on *traditions*. A tradition is a way of doing things that a family keeps for a long time.
Children help grandparents too. They carry bags. They show how a phone works. They sit and listen. Care goes both ways.

words.d: a way of doing things that a family or group keeps for a long time

look.title: Hands in the Dough
look.text: Look at two pairs of hands. Big, wrinkled hands fold a small dumpling. Small hands try the same fold. The first one is lumpy. The next one is better. The big hands clap.
look.prompt: Who is teaching? Who is learning? What could the child teach back?

choices: A way of doing things a family keeps for a long time
check.why: The reading says a tradition is a way of doing things kept for a long time.

choices: Make them do all the work
check.why: The reading says children carry bags, show how a phone works, and listen.

check.q: In the reading, what might a grandfather in Italy show a child?
check.why: The reading says a grandfather in Italy may show how to plant tomatoes.

lessons.title: Chores Help Everyone
lessons.mainIdea: When each person does a chore, the whole family is helped.
reading: At Rosa's house, the dishes pile up after dinner. Dad washes. Rosa dries. Ben puts the cups away. Soon the sink is empty.
A *chore* is a job you do at home. Chores keep a home clean and safe. Small children can do small chores. They can feed a pet or pick up toys.
When everyone helps, the work goes fast. No one has to do it all. Helping is one way to show care.

words.d: a job you do to help at home

look.title: The Chore Chart
look.text: Look at the chart on the fridge. Monday: Rosa feeds the cat. Tuesday: Ben takes out trash. Wednesday: Rosa sets the table. Thursday: Ben waters plants. A star goes by each job when it is done.
look.prompt: Pick one chore you could do. Which day would you do it?

choices: A job you do to help at home
check.why: The reading says a chore is a job you do at home.

check.q: What does Rosa do after dinner?
check.why: Dad washes, and Rosa dries the dishes.

check.q: Why does the work go fast?
check.why: The reading says when everyone helps, the work goes fast.

lessons.title: Every Family Has Its Own Ways
lessons.mainIdea: Each family has its own ways, and you can tell about yours.
reading: Mia's family eats pancakes on Saturday. Kai and his dad walk to the lake on Sunday. Lena's family sings before dinner. Each family has its own ways.
These ways are called *customs*. A custom is something a family or group does again and again. No custom is the only right one. Each one matters to that family.
You can tell about your family's ways. Say who is in your family. Say what you like to do together. Listen when friends tell about theirs.

words.d: something a family or group does again and again

look.title: A World Promise About Families
look.text: The family is the natural and fundamental group unit of society and is entitled to protection by society and the State.
look.cite: United Nations, Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 16, 1948
look.prompt: Many countries signed this promise. In your own words, what does it say families should get?

check.q: What does Lena's family do before dinner?
check.why: The reading says Lena's family sings before dinner.

choices: Something a family does again and again
check.why: The reading says a custom is something a family or group does again and again.

check.q: A friend tells about her family's ways. What can you do?
check.why: The reading says to listen when friends tell about their family's ways.

choices: A dad and one child who care for each other
review.why: A family is people who belong together and care for each other. It can be just two people.

review.q: Your cousin is the child of your ___.
review.why: A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.

review.q: Rosa's grandma, mom, and baby brother are how many generations?
review.why: Grandma, Mom, and the baby are three age groups. That is three generations.
Feeding a pet is a job that helps at home. That is a chore.

review.q: A grandmother teaches a child to fold dumplings. She is passing on a ___.
review.why: A tradition is a way of doing things a family keeps for a long time.

review.q: Two families have different customs. What is true?
choices: Each custom matters to its family
review.why: The chapter says no custom is the only right one. Each matters to its family.
